details: The bin/wt template that relay setup copies into every new project still makes wt/queue-<x> branches for a queue- name; relay's own bin/wt was fixed on 30 Oct, so every project set up from now on keeps the bug.
failing_case: A project set up by relay (bin/wt written from templates/bin-wt). The front, told by guard_main to use bin/wt new <name>, runs
bin/wt new queue-docs main there: it makes .worktrees/queue-docs on wt/queue-docs, which relay doctor lists as a leftover queue
branch and tidy and the merge hook skip as a landing branch. Expected: refused as in relay's own bin/wt.
pass_cases: 1. templates/bin-wt rendered (branch=main), run in a temp repo: new queue-docs main -> exit non-zero, stderr names "queue-",
2. Same rendered template: new docs main -> .worktrees/docs on wt/docs, exit 0, prints the path.
3. relay's own bin/wt keeps both behaviours of tests/test_bin_wt.py.
reason: Branch has no change; test tests/test_bin_wt.py:27 passes at Q1's since (fix already on master in c77fba2a), so the fail-without-fix condition cannot hold here. It does fail at c77fba2a^.

details: CONFIRMED by reading lib/relay_queue.py:1051-1067 (find_finding reads only the given JSON's findings list) and 1171-1183 (add_from
copies the finding into `add` with no look at any check of that review). The review JSON carries no verdict; the check record that
carries it (a separate file in the scratchpad and .relay/checks) is never consulted. The front skill (plugins/delegate/skills/delegate/SKILL.md:247)
tells the front to queue every outside finding with add --from, and the cycle checks fixers against outside findings too, so a fixer
that fixes an outside finding in the same change (as here) always leaves a stale item behind. Principle 2 (Waste): built into the setup,
repeats each time a fixer fixes an outside finding -> MEDIUM, fixed before the merge of the change that fixes it (outside this change).
Cost here: one queue item, one lane, one worker, one review (Opus) over an empty range. Size: 30 agent minutes.
evidence: git -C <wt> log --oneline master..HEAD -> (empty); git rev-parse HEAD master -> both 10965b21
relay check show check-bin-wt-new-queue-x-still-makes-wt-queue-x-which.json -> "templates/bin-wt:10: LOW: F1 ... Source: review-...json F1 ... Verdict: MET tests/test_bin_wt.py:45"
relay queue show the-bin-wt-... -> "found 2026-10-30T23:07:34Z in finding F1 of review-bin-wt-new-queue-x-still-makes-wt-queue-x-which.json"
git show --stat c77fba2a -> templates/bin-wt | 3 +++, tests/test_bin_wt.py | 23 ++++; merge-base --is-ancestor c77fba2a master -> on-master
python3 -m unittest tests.test_bin_wt -> Ran 4 tests OK
failing_case: Live, 31 Oct: review-bin-wt-new-queue-x-still-makes-wt-queue-x-which.json F1 (kind outside, templates/bin-wt:10). The fixer fixed it in
the same branch (c77fba2a); check-bin-wt-new-queue-x-still-makes-wt-queue-x-which.json records F1 "Verdict: MET tests/test_bin_wt.py:45".
One minute later `relay queue add --from review-...json F1` queued it as the-bin-wt-template-that-relay-setup-writes-into: accepted, no
warning. A lane was built, a worker ran, and this review ran over an empty range. Expected: refused (or warned) with a line naming the
check record that gives F1 MET and the commit that fixed it.
fix_hint: In add_from, when the report is a review, look for a check record whose findings carry `Source: <this review> F<n>` (the check JSON
already stores the source) in .relay/checks and beside the report; when one gives that finding MET, refuse with
"F<n> is MET in <check file> (fixed in <branch>); nothing to queue". Alternatively the front skill's line 247 says to queue outside
findings from the check record (which has verdicts), not from the review, and add_from refuses a MET finding of a check record.
pass_cases: 1. A review JSON with F1 outside, and a check record of the same review (its F1 sourced from that review) with F1 MET:
relay queue add --from <review.json> F1 --input why.toml -> refused, the message names the check file and "MET", no queue file written.
2. Same review, check record gives F1 NOT MET (or no check record exists): add --from queues the item as today.
3. add --from <check.json> N1 (a check's own new finding) queues as today.
4. A review JSON with F2 outside that the check marks MET while F1 is NOT MET: add --from F1 queues, add --from F2 is refused.
reason: Outside finding in lib/relay_queue.py add_from; becomes its own fix item, not part of this branch.
findings.summary: relay queue add --from <review> F<n> queues a finding that the branch's check already marked MET, so a fixed finding becomes a new lane (principle 2, waste)
